Start with the expanded examples. Open further examples for options and alternative R approaches.

dfbeta

Obtain standardized deletion influence on one slope

Stata 

dfbeta x

R stats 

stats::dfbetas(fit)[,"x"]

Differs from Stata Returns standardized coefficient-deletion diagnostics from dfbetas for x; coefficient ordering, missing rows and diagnostic naming must be aligned with the Stata model.

Stata reference · R reference

estat

Summarize variables in the actual estimation sample

Stata 

estat summarize

R tidystata 

tidystata::summ(stats::model.frame(fit))

Differs from Stata After the displayed numeric OLS model, summarizes its complete-case estimation sample with N, mean, SD, minimum and maximum; factor-variable expansions require their explicit numeric model columns.

Stata reference · R reference

Compute variance inflation factors after OLS

Stata 

estat vif

R car 

car::vif(fit)

Differs from Stata car returns ordinary VIFs for one-degree-of-freedom terms and generalized VIFs for multi-parameter terms. Stata estat vif reports column-level VIFs, so factor-term output is not directly interchangeable.

Stata reference · R reference

7 more examples and alternatives

Test heteroskedasticity against one predictor using a studentized statistic

Stata 

estat hettest x, iid

R lmtest 

lmtest::bptest(fit,varformula=~x,data=data,studentize=TRUE)

Differs from Stata Uses the studentized Koenker version of the Breusch-Pagan test, corresponding to the iid variant shown. Match the auxiliary regressors and estimation sample; the default bptest differs from default Stata hettest.

Stata reference · R reference

Run the classical Breusch-Pagan heteroskedasticity test

Stata 

estat hettest, rhs

R lmtest 

lmtest::bptest(fit,studentize=FALSE)

Differs from Stata studentize=FALSE selects the normal-theory version; default bptest uses the Koenker version.

Stata reference · R reference

Compare penalized-likelihood model criteria

Stata 

estat ic

R stats 

c(AIC=stats::AIC(fit),BIC=stats::BIC(fit))

R keeps fitted model objects; model names are fixed workflow labels.

Stata reference · R reference

Run Ramsey RESET using powers of fitted values

Stata 

estat ovtest

R lmtest 

lmtest::resettest(fit,power=2:4,type="fitted")

Differs from Stata Uses RESET powers two through four of the fitted values or regressors as shown. Regressor-factor expansion and rank-deficient auxiliary terms may differ from Stata.

Stata reference · R reference

Run RESET using powers of regressors

Stata 

estat ovtest, rhs

R lmtest 

lmtest::resettest(fit,power=2:4,type="regressor")

Differs from Stata Uses RESET powers two through four of the fitted values or regressors as shown. Regressor-factor expansion and rank-deficient auxiliary terms may differ from Stata.

lincom

Estimate the sum of two slopes with its standard error

Stata 

lincom x + z

R marginaleffects 

marginaleffects::hypotheses(fit, hypothesis = "x + z = 0", df = stats::df.residual(fit))

Differs from Stata After fit <- lm(y ~ x + z, data = data); uses named coefficients, model covariance and residual t degrees of freedom.

Stata reference · R reference

Estimate a difference of slopes with its standard error

Stata 

lincom x - z

R marginaleffects 

marginaleffects::hypotheses(fit, hypothesis = "x - z = 0", df = stats::df.residual(fit))

Differs from Stata After fit <- lm(y ~ x + z, data = data); uses named coefficients, model covariance and residual t degrees of freedom.

Stata reference · R reference

linktest

Regress an outcome on fitted values and their square

Stata 

linktest

R stats 

{ data$hat <- stats::fitted(fit); stats::lm(y ~ hat+I(hat^2),data=data) }

Shown for OLS; link tests after other model families must refit the appropriate family.

Stata reference · R reference

lrtest

Compare nested maximum-likelihood models

Stata 

lrtest reduced full

R lmtest 

lmtest::lrtest(reduced,full)

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow.

Stata reference · R reference

margins

Predict at specified covariate values

Stata 

margins, at(x=(2 3 4))

R marginaleffects 

marginaleffects::avg_predictions(fit, newdata = marginaleffects::datagrid(model = fit, x = c(2, 3, 4), grid_type = "counterfactual"), by = "x", type = "response", df = Inf)

Differs from Stata Sets x to each listed value, retaining other covariates at the estimation-sample distribution, with delta-method uncertainty.

Stata reference · R reference

Average a continuous-predictor marginal effect

Stata 

margins, dydx(x)

R marginaleffects 

marginaleffects::avg_slopes(fit, variables = "x", type = "response", df = Inf)

Differs from Stata Averages the probability-scale derivative over the model sample with delta-method uncertainty and normal inference.

Stata reference · R reference

Evaluate a marginal effect at mean covariates

Stata 

margins, dydx(x) atmeans

R marginaleffects 

marginaleffects::slopes(fit, variables = "x", newdata = "mean", type = "response", df = Inf)

Differs from Stata After logit b x z: derivative at the estimation-sample numeric predictor means, with delta-method uncertainty.

Stata reference · R reference

Obtain forecast standard errors including residual variance

Stata 

predict result, stdf

R stats 

data$result <- sqrt(stats::predict(fit,se.fit=TRUE)$se.fit^2+summary(fit)$sigma^2)

Differs from Stata Adds residual variance to the squared standard error of the fitted OLS mean. This is a standard error for a new individual prediction, not the fitted mean; assumes homoskedastic errors and matching model sample.

Stata reference · R reference

roccomp

Compare paired marker ROC areas using DeLong inference

Stata 

roccomp b x z

R pROC 

{ sample <- stats::na.omit(data[c("b", "x", "z")]); pROC::roc.test(pROC::roc(sample$b, sample$x, levels = c(0, 1), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE), pROC::roc(sample$b, sample$z, levels = c(0, 1), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE), paired = TRUE, method = "delong") }

Differs from Stata Paired DeLong AUC equality test on common complete cases with fixed larger-marker case direction.

Stata reference · R reference

roctab

Estimate a nonparametric ROC area for a marker

Stata 

roctab b x

R pROC 

pROC::roc(data$b, data$x, levels = c(0, 1), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE, ci = TRUE, ci.method = "delong")

Differs from Stata Larger markers indicate cases; computes empirical AUC and its DeLong normal interval.

Stata reference · R reference

Tabulate sensitivity and specificity across ROC thresholds

Stata 

roctab b x, detail

R pROC 

pROC::coords(pROC::roc(data$b,data$x,levels=c(0,1),direction="<",quiet=TRUE),x="all",ret=c("threshold","sensitivity","specificity"))

Differs from Stata Returns all pROC thresholds with sensitivity and specificity for explicit event direction. Threshold locations and endpoint conventions differ from Stata roctab detail cutpoints.

Stata reference · R reference

test

Test a single regression coefficient

Stata 

test x = 0

R car 

car::linearHypothesis(fit,"x = 0")

Differs from Stata Tests the specified coefficient restriction on the existing fit. car selects its reference statistic from the model class; a GLM chi-square test differs from the OLS F test used by Stata regress postestimation.

Stata reference · R reference

Test equality of two regression slopes

Stata 

test x = z

R car 

car::linearHypothesis(fit,"x = z")

Differs from Stata Tests the specified coefficient restriction on the existing fit. car selects its reference statistic from the model class; a GLM chi-square test differs from the OLS F test used by Stata regress postestimation.

Stata reference · R reference

Jointly test two regression coefficients

Stata 

test x z

R car 

car::linearHypothesis(fit,c("x = 0","z = 0"))

Differs from Stata Tests the specified coefficient restriction on the existing fit. car selects its reference statistic from the model class; a GLM chi-square test differs from the OLS F test used by Stata regress postestimation.

Stata reference · R reference

testnl

Test an exponentiated coefficient with a nonlinear Wald test

Stata 

testnl exp(_b[x]) = 1

R car 

{ d <- car::deltaMethod(fit,"exp(x)"); w <- ((d$Estimate-1)/d$SE)^2; c(chisq=w,p.value=stats::pchisq(w,df=1,lower.tail=FALSE)) }

Differs from Stata Forms a one-degree-of-freedom Wald chi-square from a first-order delta-method standard error. The R vector omits Stata coefficient and confidence-interval output.

Stata reference · R reference

testparm

Jointly test a categorical predictor

Stata 

testparm i.g

R car 

car::linearHypothesis(fit,c("g6 = 0","g8 = 0"))

Differs from Stata The restrictions name the fitted factor coefficients explicitly. Different reference levels or contrasts require different coefficient names; this is not an automatic expansion of any Stata factor-variable expression.
